items.headline: CISA adds actively exploited Perforce Puppet RCE flaw CVE-2026-115731 to KEV
items.summary: The Hacker News: CISA has added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing reports of active exploitation. The critical flaw (CVSS 9.4) affects Perforce Puppet, a platform for infrastructure-as-code and configuration management. Because Puppet servers push configuration to the machines they manage, a compromise could give attackers broad control. SecurityWeek: A critical flaw in Perforce Puppet, CVE-2026-115731, lets any client holding a CA-signed agent certificate execute code on the Puppet server.
items.importance_rationale: This is a new KEV entry for actively exploited, widely deployed enterprise management software.
items.detection_coverage_note: The source links no detection rules. In our assessment, teams should monitor Puppet server logs, catalog changes and unexpected processes on Puppet servers.
items.recommended_action: Patch Puppet servers right away and restrict network access to them. Review recent configuration changes for signs of tampering. SecurityWeek: Review which certificates have been issued to agents, revoke any you don't recognise, and hunt for signs of compromise.

items.summary: KrebsOnSecurity reports that at least 178 major websites served data-stealing malware to visitors over a 24-hour period through a weakness involving Optimizely. items.headline: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package compromised to deliver cloud credential stealer
items.summary: Multiple security vendors report that malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package were published on November 17, 2026. items.recommended_action: Find and remove agent-framework versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. Rotate any cloud credentials that were reachable from affected hosts or CI environments. Pin dependencies to verified versions.

items.headline: Critical unauthenticated RCE "Java4Shell" in OpenJDK runtime (CVE-2026-114938)
items.summary: Qualys ThreatPROTECT: Qualys reports a critical flaw in the OpenJDK runtime, CVE-2026-114938, that can let unauthenticated attackers execute code remotely. Because it sits in the runtime itself, services may be exposed even if their applications and libraries are not flawed. The advisory's URL refers to threat actors exploiting it, but the summary gives no exploitation details, so this needs verification. GreyNoise Blog: GreyNoise is monitoring scanning and exploitation attempts against the Java4Shell OpenJDK Base64 decoder flaw. Observed attempts show attacker interest, but the source does not confirm any successful compromise. Qualys Vulnerabilities and Threat Research: Qualys details Java4Shell, a memory-corruption flaw in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder rated 9.2 (CVSS v4) by researchers and 8.1 (CVSS v3.1) by Oracle. Unauthenticated attackers may corrupt heap memory, leak secrets and achieve remote code execution; researchers demonstrated pre-auth RCE. Cisco Talos, CERT-EU Security Advisories: On 17 November 2026, Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes for CVE-2026-114938. Talos reports a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 for the flaw. It could allow unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions. The sources do not report exploitation in the wild. Help Net Security: Oracle and the OpenJDK project patched CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption bug in the Base64 decoder that could let unauthenticated attackers run code on servers hosting Java applications. Researchers say exploitation is tricky and depends on specific CPUs. There is no evidence of successful attacks yet, but CISA urges organizations to patch immediately. The Hacker News: Oracle planned to release patches on November 17, 2026 for 11 Java SE vulnerabilities. All can be exploited remotely without authentication, with a maximum CVSS score of 8.1. Separate reports describe a potentially critical OpenJDK remote code execution flaw; no exploitation has been reported. Amazon Linux Security Center: A memory-corruption flaw in the OpenJDK Base64 decoder affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 systems with certain CPU capabilities; ARM64 is not affected. Depending on the deployment, it could let unauthenticated users crash the JVM or, in some environments, let an authenticated low-privileged user run code. Oracle has patched versions 17, 21, 25 and 27, and no exploitation has been reported.
items.importance_rationale: No source-reported exploitation or recent KEV evidence; vulnerability capped at high.
items.detection_coverage_note: The source links no detection rules. Our assessment is that defenders should watch for unexpected child processes spawned by Java services and for unusual outbound connections from them.
items.recommended_action: List all OpenJDK installations, including bundled runtimes. Apply vendor fixes as soon as they are available, putting internet-facing Java services first. Cisco Talos, CERT-EU Security Advisories: Inventory Java runtimes, including those bundled inside applications. Patch internet-facing applications first, since the exact conditions for exploitation are not yet clear. Help Net Security: How exploitable this is in practice is still unclear. The Hacker News: Inventory your Java SE and OpenJDK runtimes and apply the Oracle and distribution updates. Amazon Linux Security Center: Find x86-64 hosts running OpenJDK 17.0.6 or later and apply the vendor's updates for 17, 21, 25 or 27. Prioritise services that decode untrusted Base64 input.

items.recommended_action: Review Workspace sign-in and data-access logs, and enforce phishing-resistant MFA. Treat messages from compromised partners with extra scrutiny. Full details are limited in the source.
items.model_importance_rationale: A nation-state espionage campaign using cloud compromise for third-party intrusion against US organizations. The victims' sectors are not stated as critical infrastructure.

items.headline: Physical attack resets TPM lockout, letting short Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs be guessed
items.summary: Researchers at TU Berlin say someone who opens the case of an AMD-based PC, or of some Intel-based PCs, can reset the TPM anti-hammering lockout. items.recommended_action: Require longer or alphanumeric BitLocker pre-boot PINs and Windows Hello PINs on laptops. Review how lost or stolen devices are handled, and watch for vendor firmware guidance.
